evidence.reason: ENTRY uses a conventional top bar (logo left, five text links centred, search and theme toggle right) over a centred hero with headline, one-line value copy, primary/secondary button pair and an install command. evidence.reason: DETAIL shows a summary (title, description, tag, demo) and defers depth to install tabs (npm/pnpm/yarn/bun x React/Vue/Svelte/Vanilla), a collapsed 'Copy for AI' dropdown and a 'Controls' button. INTERACTION keeps 'Copy for AI' and 'Share' collapsed; DISCOVERY mobile folds the category sidebar into a 'Browse the library' accordion.

INTERACTION has actions beyond navigation (slider controls, Reset, copy buttons, Copy for AI, Share) but no post-click state was captured; the only interaction captures are hover (search button gains a ring; 'Get started' dims slightly) and focus. Whether copying or resetting produces immediate visible feedback cannot be seen.

The site loads live canvas/WebGL demos and a 166-card grid, so loading states are relevant, but no in-progress load was captured. DISCOVERY-desktop.png shows ~14,000 px of blank page between the first nine cards and the footer with no placeholders, which may be deferred rendering rather than a captured loading state, so it cannot be judged as a designed state either way.
No form exists on any captured surface; the only text inputs are single search fields and the INTERACTION control sliders, and no form-submit capture was produced. na_condition (no form) is met.

The INTERACTION controls panel has a small text 'Reset' action that discards the user's tuned values, which is the only candidate destructive action; no capture shows whether it confirms or offers undo. No other destructive actions appear on any surface.

The first ENTRY screen states the value ('See every component running live, tune it with visual controls, then copy the code'), offers 'Get started' and 'Browse components', and immediately shows a one-line install command with a copy button; the mobile first screen keeps headline, copy and both buttons above the fold.

A search over 166 components necessarily has a no-results state, but no empty state was captured (all DISCOVERY captures show '166 of 166 components'). The DETAIL fallback notice is a degraded-rendering message, not an empty state.

Help is inline at the point of doubt: DETAIL places 'Move the lens over the photo to magnify every detail.' under the demo heading and a dismissible notice explaining the fallback rendering with the exact Chrome flag and a copy button; INTERACTION shows the component description under its thumbnail; ENTRY labels the install command 'ONE COMMAND'. No tour is used.
No multi-step flow appears on any surface; install is a single command and the playground is a single screen. na_condition is met.
No testimonials or quotes appear on ENTRY, DISCOVERY, DETAIL or INTERACTION; the only attribution text is the curator note and the footer credit line, neither of which is a testimonial.

The only numbers presented are exact catalogue counts ('166 components' in the sidebar, '166 of 166 components' above the grid, '166 components' in the mobile accordion), which are specific and directly backed by the list they describe; no vague quantities ('thousands', 'many') are used.

No pricing or signup surface exists; the product is an install-by-command library and the captured surfaces contain no purchase or account decision point, so na_condition (no decision point: pricing/signup) is met. No logos, ratings or badges appear anywhere either.
No surface collects user data: there are no signup, payment or contact forms, only local search inputs and playground sliders. na_condition (no data collected) is met.
